_README: Benchmark for the F4 Rashba coefficient (rashba.py, T2-1). The core TB models a [001]-polar (P4mm) CsBX3 with a rigid sublattice displacement; we compare its bulk Rashba alpha_R to a verified BULK DFT value for an inorganic polar perovskite. Surface-Rashba measurements are explicitly EXCLUDED (different system).

bulk_dft_reference.material: CsPbF3 (ferroelectric R3c, inorganic -- closest to the Cs-based core TB)
bulk_dft_reference.source: P. Bhumla, D. Gill, S. Sheoran, S. Bhattacharya, 'Origin of Rashba Spin-Splitting and Strain Tunability in Ferroelectric Bulk CsPbF3', arXiv:2108.03683 (2021) (verified web 2026-05-24).
bulk_dft_reference.note: Inorganic Cs perovskite, BULK polar phase -- the appropriate comparison class for the Kashikar Cs-based TB. CBM Rashba (1.05) > VBM (0.41).

surface_reference_excluded.source: D. Niesner et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 117, 126401 (2016)
surface_reference_excluded.why_excluded: This is a SURFACE Rashba measurement, not the bulk polar phase the TB models; not a valid magnitude benchmark for a bulk calculation.

tb_results.note: alpha_R grows ~linearly with the polar displacement (0.007 at 0.1 -> 0.049 at 0.8).

comparison.qualitative_sign_structure: MATCH (category C): cubic Pm-3m gives alpha_R=0 (Kramers), the [001] polar P4mm gives alpha_R != 0 with spin-momentum locking; and the CBM Rashba dominates over the VBM, as in the CsPbF3 DFT (CBM>VBM).
comparison.absolute_magnitude: TB CBM alpha_R ~0.027 eVA vs bulk DFT ~1.05 eVA -> TB UNDERESTIMATES by ~40x. Does NOT reach order-of-magnitude agreement. Category D.
comparison.honest_note: The TB polar model is a crude RIGID sublattice displacement (displacement parameter uncalibrated to a real ferroelectric distortion/polarization), and the SK-TB velocity/position operator lacks covalent (Blount) corrections, so the absolute Rashba strength is strongly underestimated. Only the sign, spin-locking, and CBM>VBM ordering are claimed; the absolute alpha_R is not reproduced (consistent with the module's standing honest caveat).
